readings.title: A workshop for changing careers
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content:
A careers centre offered a workshop to adults changing jobs. Many participants brought useful experience but did not know how to describe it. The main obstacle was job histories written only as task lists. Applicants named duties without showing what they had improved or learned. At first, the people involved did not agree on which part of the proposal deserved the most attention.

To investigate, the team used a review of anonymised application examples. Advisers asked participants to connect past actions with results and transferable skills. The organizers kept the first stage small enough to change without wasting substantial time or resources.

The evidence indicated specific examples made experience clearer. The repeated observations mattered more than one unusual experience and changed how the team understood the situation. The group then introduced short achievement notes alongside work history. The revised approach was explained to users and given a date for a further practical check. The records were useful because they described ordinary use rather than an ideal situation imagined at a meeting.

The case suggests a broader point: career change requires translation of existing skills. The experience connected a small local decision with a wider need to listen, measure and adjust. The group published its reasons so that people who preferred a different result could still understand the choice. For those taking part in a workshop for changing careers, the value of the work lay in connecting a specific observation to a visible decision. People could question the result because the process had been explained. No single trial could settle every issue. The group planned to keep listening after the new arrangement began and to compare later experiences with its first records. This gradual approach allowed the organizers to protect the original aim while changing a method that had not worked as expected in everyday use.

readings.title: Learning equipment at a new job
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content:
A warehouse trained new employees to use a scanning device. Trainees passed a demonstration but struggled during a busy shift. The main obstacle was practice limited to ideal conditions. The class showed a clean sample label but not damaged or unusually placed labels. The question mattered to people with different schedules and levels of experience, so one account could not represent everyone.

To investigate, the team used supervised observation during ordinary work. Qualified trainers recorded which situations caused hesitation without rushing new staff. A simple record of what happened each day gave the team a starting point for comparison.

The evidence indicated varied examples improved readiness. The repeated observations mattered more than one unusual experience and changed how the team understood the situation. The group then introduced practice with common exceptions before independent use. The revised approach was explained to users and given a date for a further practical check. Some participants welcomed the change immediately, while others noticed practical details that needed further work.

The case suggests a broader point: training should prepare people for realistic variation. The experience connected a small local decision with a wider need to listen, measure and adjust. The result was a revised plan, not a claim that every difficulty had disappeared. For those taking part in learning equipment at a new job, the value of the work lay in connecting a specific observation to a visible decision. People could question the result because the process had been explained. No single trial could settle every issue. The group planned to keep listening after the new arrangement began and to compare later experiences with its first records. This gradual approach allowed the organizers to protect the original aim while changing a method that had not worked as expected in everyday use.

readings.title: Finding an apprenticeship placement
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content:
A college advertised apprenticeships on a noticeboard. Students visiting after evening classes often discovered that deadlines had passed. The main obstacle was opportunities posted without current dates. Old notices stayed in place and looked as important as new ones. The initial idea sounded reasonable, yet the details of the place made it harder to carry out than expected.

To investigate, the team used a check of listings and student visits. The careers team compared posting dates with application deadlines and asked students how they searched. Instead of relying on a single opinion, the team invited several users to describe what they actually did.

The evidence indicated a dated list improved planning. The repeated observations mattered more than one unusual experience and changed how the team understood the situation. The group then introduced weekly updates with clear closing dates. The revised approach was explained to users and given a date for a further practical check. This allowed the organizers to separate a temporary inconvenience from a pattern that required attention.

The case suggests a broader point: career information loses value when it is stale. The experience connected a small local decision with a wider need to listen, measure and adjust. They also decided when to check the arrangement again, because conditions could change over time. For those taking part in finding an apprenticeship placement, the value of the work lay in connecting a specific observation to a visible decision. People could question the result because the process had been explained. No single trial could settle every issue. The group planned to keep listening after the new arrangement began and to compare later experiences with its first records. This gradual approach allowed the organizers to protect the original aim while changing a method that had not worked as expected in everyday use.

readings.title: Feedback after a practice interview
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content:
A training group ran mock interviews. Some learners received a score but could not tell which answer needed improvement. The main obstacle was feedback reduced to a single number. Two participants with the same score had different strengths and difficulties. The people affected were invited to comment before a permanent arrangement was chosen.

To investigate, the team used a review of recorded practice answers. Coaches identified one example of clear communication and one next step for each learner. The first trial produced both useful results and questions the team could not yet answer.

The evidence indicated specific comments led to better second attempts. The repeated observations mattered more than one unusual experience and changed how the team understood the situation. The group then introduced short written feedback linked to an example. The revised approach was explained to users and given a date for a further practical check. Rather than hide those limits, the public note explained how the next version had been selected.

The case suggests a broader point: evaluation should support the next effort. The experience connected a small local decision with a wider need to listen, measure and adjust. That explanation made later changes easier to discuss with residents and staff. For those taking part in feedback after a practice interview, the value of the work lay in connecting a specific observation to a visible decision. People could question the result because the process had been explained. No single trial could settle every issue. The group planned to keep listening after the new arrangement began and to compare later experiences with its first records. This gradual approach allowed the organizers to protect the original aim while changing a method that had not worked as expected in everyday use.

translation.stem:
Translate the following passage into Chinese:
A useful plan for career development and practical training must take account of the people who will use it. An idea may look complete on paper and still create difficulties during an ordinary week. Organizers therefore tried the local career skills programme on a small scale and invited comments from users with different schedules. They recorded benefits as well as the time and resources needed to provide them. Some findings supported the original aim, while others suggested that the method should change. The group published both kinds of result instead of presenting the trial as a simple success or failure. This allowed residents to discuss the next step with a clearer understanding of its possible effects.

translation.referenceAnswer: 关于职业发展与技能培训的有用方案必须考虑实际使用它的人。一个想法在纸上看似完整，平常使用时却仍可能出现困难。因此，组织者小规模试行该服务，并邀请时间安排不同的使用者提出意见。他们既记录益处，也记录提供这些益处所需的时间和资源。有些发现支持最初目标，另一些则表明方法应当调整。团队同时公布两类结果，而没有把试行简单说成成功或失败。这让居民能更清楚地了解可能的影响，再讨论下一步。

writing.stem: Write at least 100 words in English to the skills development team about a community activity related to career development and practical training. Explain how different people can participate, what should be recorded, and how the results should be shared.
writing.explanation: 范文供考生自评，注意任务要点、组织结构及语言准确性。
writing.sampleAnswer:
Dear Committee Members,
I would like to propose a small improvement to the local career skills programme. People have noticed job histories written only as task lists, and a short trial could help us understand how often this problem occurs. We should ask regular users and people who have not used the service before to describe their experiences. Their comments may reveal details that a plan made in an office would miss.
For one month, staff could keep a simple record of participation, time spent and any difficulties reported. We should also explain the purpose of the trial in clear language so that residents know how to contribute. After the month, please publish a brief summary of both benefits and limits. The final decision should be based on what people actually experienced, with a date for checking the arrangement again.
Yours sincerely,
A resident
